facts.raw_span: A 64-year-old woman presented with a slowly enlarging mass in the left labia majora over 10 years
the mass was firm, painless, immobile, and measured approximately 7 × 4 cm, extending toward the mons pubis
Her vital signs were normal
Routine laboratory tests were normal
histopathology in 2007 showed chondroid syringoma
histology showed clear cell hidradenoma
ultrasound revealed a 4.2 × 8 cm heterogeneous, hypervascular subcutaneous mass
CT scan demonstrated a 3.8 × 7.2 cm heterogeneous, contrast-enhancing lesion in the left labia majora extending to the anterior perineum
a low-density focus in the liver suggestive of a simple cyst
The vulvar mass was excised; on gross examination it measured 7 × 3 × 4 cm, was gray and well-circumscribed
was reported again as chondroid syringoma
The patient noted another recurrence near the fourchette

concepts.why: The patient's mass was reported as chondroid syringoma on two separate occasions, suggesting a strong likelihood of this diagnosis.
The patient's histology showed clear cell hidradenoma, which is a rare tumor that can present as a slowly enlarging mass.

rationales.F06: Clear cell hidradenoma histology supports C02

frontier_selector.rationale: Multiple histopathology reports confirming chondroid syringoma, including the most recent examination.
